title: Glass: identification and prep
identification: Container glass (jars, bottles) is hard, cold to the touch, rings when tapped and is heavier than plastic of the same size.
Look for a seam line on the side and embossed letters or numbers on the base.
Drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors, ovenware and ceramics look similar but melt at different temperatures and are not container glass.
cleaning_prep: Empty and rinse out food; a quick rinse is enough, spotless is not required.
Remove metal lids and plastic caps and recycle them separately.
Labels can usually stay on; soak them off only if you plan to reuse the jar.

recycling.stream: Glass bottle bank or the glass section of a recycling point

notes: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
In the UAE, glass collection varies by emirate and community: many malls, supermarkets and residential areas have separate glass or mixed recycling bins, so check the label on the bin.
Never bag glass inside plastic bags at a bottle bank.
donation: Clean jars with working lids are often welcome at refill and zero-waste shops, home cooks and community kitchens.
Chipped or cracked jars should not be donated for food use.

title: Plastic: identification and prep
identification: Look for the resin code: a number from 1 to 7 inside a triangle of arrows, usually on the base.
PET (1) is clear and crinkly; HDPE (2) is opaque and waxy; PP (5) is stiff and often used for tubs and caps.
Soft films and bags stretch when pulled; rigid plastics snap or crack.
cleaning_prep: Empty and rinse bottles and tubs; food residue contaminates whole bales of plastic.
Squash bottles flat to save space and put the cap back on unless local instructions say otherwise.
Keep films and bags separate from rigid plastics.

not_accepted: plastic bags and films in most kerbside bins
containers that held chemicals, oil or pesticides

notes: Codes 1, 2 and 5 are the most widely recycled; 3, 6 and 7 rarely are.
Never burn plastic at home or in a yard: the smoke is toxic.
Many UAE supermarkets collect clean plastic bags and some offer collection points for bottles; check the store.
donation: Clean food tubs and sturdy containers are often wanted by schools, nurseries and art groups for craft and storage.
Clear clamshell boxes are useful to community gardens as seed trays.

title: Paper and cardboard: identification and prep
identification: Corrugated cardboard has a wavy middle layer; paperboard (cereal boxes) is thin and flat.
Newsprint is soft and grey-toned; magazines and flyers are glossy but still recyclable.
Paper cups, receipts and wax or foil-lined wrappers look like paper but contain plastic, wax or chemicals.
cleaning_prep: Keep paper dry and clean; wet or greasy paper spoils a whole batch.
Flatten boxes and remove plastic tape, windows and bubble wrap where you can.
Tear off greasy parts of pizza boxes and compost or bin them.
notes: Paper fibres can be recycled about five to seven times before they become too short.
Cardboard is often collected separately at malls, supermarkets and residential buildings in the UAE.
donation: Clean boxes are useful to people moving house and to small online sellers.
Schools and nurseries often take cardboard tubes, egg cartons and magazines for art projects.

title: Metal: identification and prep
identification: A magnet sticks to steel (tin cans, jar lids) but not to aluminium (drink cans, foil trays).
Aluminium is very light and crushes easily; steel cans are heavier and stiffer.
Pressurised aerosol cans have a nozzle and warning labels and need separate handling.
cleaning_prep: Rinse cans and trays so no food is left.
Push the lid of an opened can inside it, or tape the edge, to avoid cuts.
Scrunch clean foil into a ball at least the size of a fist so it can be sorted.

accepted: metal jar lids and bottle tops
not_accepted: aerosol cans that are not empty

notes: Aluminium and steel can be recycled indefinitely, and recycling aluminium saves most of the energy needed to make it new.
Larger scrap metal such as old pans, rods and brackets can go to scrap metal dealers, which are common in UAE industrial areas.
donation: Clean cans and lids are useful for school craft sessions; tape or file the rims first.
Pots, pans and tools in working order can be donated through charity shops and community groups.

title: Textiles: identification and prep
identification: Check the care label for fibre content: cotton, polyester, wool or a blend.
Denim is a thick twill cotton; jersey (T-shirts) stretches and curls when cut.
Shoes, bags and belts can usually go with textiles if they are paired and dry.
cleaning_prep: Wash and dry items before donating or recycling them.
Tie shoes together in pairs and put clothes in a closed bag so they stay clean.
Separate wet, oily or moldy textiles: they cannot be reused or recycled.

recycling.stream: Textile recycling or clothing collection bin
accepted: clothes in any condition if clean and dry
not_accepted: items soaked in oil or chemicals
carpets and mattresses in most bins

notes: Worn-out textiles are shredded into insulation, stuffing and industrial rags, so torn items still have value.
Clothing collection bins run by charities and recyclers are common in UAE residential areas and malls.
donation: Wearable clothes with no holes, heavy stains or strong smells can go to clothing donation bins, charity shops and community drives.
Worn but clean fabric suits textile recycling bins or animal shelters (as bedding), rather than donation for wearing.

title: Wood: identification and prep
identification: Solid wood shows continuous grain on the edges; particle board and MDF show compressed chips or fibres.
Pallets carry an IPPC stamp: HT means heat treated, MB means methyl bromide fumigation.
Painted, varnished or pressure-treated wood (greenish tint) is handled differently from clean wood.
cleaning_prep: Remove nails, screws and metal fittings where possible.
Keep clean untreated wood separate from painted or treated wood.
Brush off soil and let wet wood dry before storing it indoors.

recycling.stream: Wood collection at a recycling centre or bulky-waste collection
not_accepted: wood soaked in oil or chemicals in general bins

notes: Never burn painted, varnished or treated wood: the smoke is toxic.
Many UAE municipalities offer bulky-waste pickup for furniture; check your emirate's municipality service.
donation: Pallets and crates are often wanted by gardeners, makers and small shops.
Solid wood furniture in good condition can go to charity shops and community groups.

title: Electronics (e-waste): identification and prep
identification: Anything with a plug, a battery, a circuit board or a screen is e-waste: phones, chargers, cables, toys with lights, small appliances.
Phones, laptops, tablets, vapes and power banks contain lithium batteries that can catch fire if damaged.
cleaning_prep: Back up and wipe personal data, then factory-reset phones and computers.
Remove removable batteries and tape their terminals.
Keep cables and chargers together in a bag.

not_accepted: loose damaged lithium batteries without taped terminals

notes: E-waste contains valuable metals and toxic substances such as lead and mercury, so it must never go to landfill.
In the UAE, many electronics retailers and malls host e-waste collection boxes, and some brands run take-back programmes.
donation: Working devices can be donated or passed on after a factory reset; some retailers accept trade-ins.
Swollen, cracked or leaking devices must go to e-waste collection, never to donation.

title: Household hazardous waste: identification and prep
identification: Hazard symbols (flame, skull, corrosion, exclamation mark) or words such as flammable, toxic, corrosive or keep out of reach of children.
Common examples: batteries, aerosol cans, paint and solvents, pesticides, bleach and strong cleaners, motor oil, medicines, fluorescent bulbs.
cleaning_prep: Keep products in their original containers with the labels on.
Never mix different chemicals, even in the same bag.
Close lids tightly and stand containers upright in a box for transport.
notes: Heat raises the risk: never leave aerosols, batteries or chemicals in a parked car during UAE summers.
Ask your municipality or a large supermarket about hazardous waste drop-off days and points.
donation: Unopened, in-date cleaning products or paint can sometimes be given to community groups; never donate opened chemicals or medicines.

title: Organic waste: identification and prep
identification: Food scraps, fruit and vegetable peels, coffee grounds, tea leaves, eggshells, garden trimmings and dry leaves.
Cooked food, meat, dairy and oil are organic but attract pests in home compost.
cleaning_prep: Keep organic waste free of plastic stickers, bags and packaging.
Drain liquids and chop large pieces so they break down faster.

recycling.stream: Compost or organic waste collection where available

notes: Food waste in landfill produces methane; composting turns it into soil.
Balcony composting works in the UAE if the bin is shaded and kept moist.
donation: Surplus unopened food that is still in date can go to community fridges and food-sharing groups.

title: Mixed and other materials: identification and prep
identification: Items made of several bonded materials (juice cartons, blister packs, crisp packets, padded envelopes) or materials such as ceramics, rubber and cork.
If parts can be separated by hand (a lid, a handle, a label), separate them first.
cleaning_prep: Separate what you can into single materials.
Rinse food packaging and keep it dry.

recycling.stream: Check locally: specialist collection or general waste
accepted: drink cartons where carton collection exists
not_accepted: bonded mixed materials in single-material bins

notes: When in doubt, keep it out: one wrong item can contaminate a whole recycling load.
Reuse is often the best route for mixed items that are hard to recycle.
donation: Items in good working order (ceramic dishes, rubber mats, cork boards) can go to charity shops or community swaps.
